content:
Fundraiser by David Xia : Fighting for legal fairness
David Xia and 2 others are organizing this fundraiser.
Supporting Yeliang Xia with donation for legal defence against the evil fugitive billionaire Wengui Guo (most wanted by Interpol)
Mr. Yeliang Xia, a former professor at Peking University and a political dissident from China.
Mr. Xia has been sued for his inquiries and criticism through TV and twitter on Guo’s so-called exposure of top confidential information in China by Wengui Guo (aka Miles Kwok, a notorious Chinese billionaire and fugitive escaped from China in 2015 and Guo got RED NOTICE twice from INTERPOL) at Eastern District Court of Virginia.
Guo hired a gang of cyber accessories and made up tons of rumors to smear Mr. Xia and Xia’s family members while filing a complaint against Xia with an accusation of defamation and a claim of five million US $ for compensation.
Guo has been abusing legal resources in US with more than 41 lawsuits for defamation undergoing and he claimed that he planned to sue more than 91 persons for the accusation of defamation.
Mr. Xia and many other defendants can’t afford to hire a qualified and experienced attorney to defend themselves. Thus, with suggestions by many web bystanders, Xia started a campaign to collect donation for legal fees against Guo.
Xia will use those donations only for the purpose of the lawsuit and he has been supported by several volunteers to work on collection, bookkeeping and supervision of donations. The goal has been set to 100,000 US$, and an individual account of GoFundMe was set up as a major channel for donation.
Please contact Julia Lee and other volunteers through [email redacted] for the details.
We’re most grateful to your attention, encouragement, support and great help!
原北大教授、政治异议人士，现时政/财经新闻评论人夏业良先生（美国之音/自由亚洲电台/博讯/新唐人等媒体）因网络质疑和评论，而被中国逃亡商人郭文贵花钱组织围攻/抹黑，并在美国弗吉尼亚东区联邦法院提交所谓诽谤指控和滥诉。
夏先生通过电视节目和推特对郭的所谓爆料（包括最高机密信息）进行了质疑和批评，郭雇佣组织了对夏及其家人的网络围攻，同时指控夏对他进行诽谤并索赔五百万美元。
郭滥用美国司法资源， 目前正在进行中的诉讼超过41起，郭宣称他计划起诉至少91位对他进行诽谤的个人。
夏先生和其他被告均无力承担雇佣合格并有经验的律师之花费。因此在众多网络旁观者的建议下开始了募捐应对郭之诉讼的律师费用。
夏先生将把募捐得款只用于本案诉讼之中，并且得到若干志愿者的支持和帮助，他们协助收集募捐款项/记账与募捐监督等工作。本次募捐活动的目标已设定为十万美元，并且已经开设了一个名为“GoFundMe”之软件的募捐账户平台以作为主要募捐渠道。
请各位捐助者通过电子邮箱：[email redacted] 与Julia Lee等志愿者联系，以获得相关细节。

content:
Fundraiser for Silkroad Uyghur by Sarah Elder : Help our local Uyghur restaurant!
Sarah Elder is organizing this fundraiser on behalf of Silkroad Uyghur.
In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville. The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare.
Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region.
Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.'
But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia.
Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! Rehmet! (Uyghur for 'thank you')

summary: Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser. The Contemporary Uyghur An
content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

content:
Fundraiser by Gulnisa Nazarova : Honoring My Mother Through an Uyghur Cookbook
An Uyghur cookbook project preserving recipes, stories, photos, and print costs
Gulnisa Nazarova is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Gulnisa Nazarova, and I have been an Uyghur language instructor for over 20 years. This year, as I turn 60, instead of gifts I am asking for something much closer to my heart.
My dear mother taught me how to cook. Through her hands, I learned patience, generosity, and how food carries memory. Many of the dishes she passed on come from the Uyghur tradition, a cuisine rich in history, flavor, and storytelling, yet still too little known and increasingly at risk of being forgotten.
This fundraiser supports a lifelong dream of mine: creating a cookbook dedicated to Uyghur cuisine and cultural heritage.
My connection to Uyghur culture begins with my family and upbringing. My parents and ancestors came from the Uyghur Autonomous Region, known as Eastern Turkistan to Soviet Central Asia in the mid-20th century, carrying with them their traditions, food, language, history, and stories. I grew up learning not only recipes, but also their deeper meaning — meals that bring families together, celebrations filled with memory, and dishes that carry history from one generation to the next.
Over the years, I have worked professionally to support Uyghur language and culture through teaching, writing, and sharing my knowledge with others around the world. This cookbook, however, is different. It comes directly from the heart — from meals shared with my family and from a deep desire to preserve the taste of home for future generations.
This is a personal initiative, and the funds raised will help cover:
Research and documentation of recipes and food stories
Whether you give a little or a lot, you are helping keep a culinary heritage alive.
Thank you for celebrating my 60th birthday by honoring my mother’s legacy with me.

content:
Fundraiser by Craig De Meillon : Support Craig’s Mission to Aid Nepal Tibet Mudslide Victims
Craig’s campaign funds deployment, equipment, and communications for mudslide rescue work
Craig De Meillon is organizing this fundraiser.
My name is Craig De Meillon, and I am based in Miami, Florida. I work in safety and emergency management and am a trained firefighter and EMT with professional experience responding to disasters, emergencies, and humanitarian situations.
I am raising these funds as an independent volunteer to support my deployment to the areas affected by the recent mudslides and flooding in Nepal near the China border. I am not a family member or representative of anyone affected by the disaster, nor am I collecting these funds on behalf of a government agency or other organization. I am responding independently based on my emergency-response experience and my ability to bring useful communications and search equipment into the field.
The funds raised will be used primarily to cover the direct costs of my deployment and emergency-response work. This includes my airfare and ground transportation to and within the affected region, accommodation and essential field logistics, food and other necessary expenses while deployed, and emergency-response equipment and supplies.
A significant part of the funding will also be used for search and communications capabilities. This may include purchasing or renting drones that can be used to conduct aerial searches, assess inaccessible areas, locate people who may be stranded or missing, and help response teams understand conditions on the ground. Funds will also be used for satellite communications equipment and associated Starlink service costs so that I can maintain reliable communications in areas where local telecommunications infrastructure may be damaged, unavailable, or overloaded.
Where practical, I may purchase essential supplies locally rather than transporting them from the United States. This allows funds to be used more efficiently and can also support local businesses and responders.
The primary beneficiary of this fundraiser is me, Craig De Meillon, because the funds are being raised to cover the actual expenses I incur while independently deploying and carrying out this emergency-response work. The money is not being raised for personal profit or general living expenses. It is intended to offset the costs directly associated with the mission, including travel, equipment, communications, transportation, and necessary field expenses.
Once on the ground, I will coordinate as appropriate with local emergency responders, humanitarian organizations, community leaders, and other response personnel to determine where my skills, equipment, and communications capabilities can be most useful. My role and activities may change depending on the needs identified in the affected areas and the accessibility and safety of the region.
I will keep records of mission-related expenses and provide updates throughout the deployment so donors can understand how the funds are being used and what work is being carried out on the ground.
Thank you to everyone who contributes, shares this fundraiser, or supports the response in any way. Every contribution helps make it possible for me to get the equipment, communications, and resources needed to reach affected areas and assist where I can. Flood

content:
Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund
Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods
KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc.
KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.
Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.
Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:
• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School
• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School
We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.
We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.
For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.
• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities
• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses
• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers
Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.
You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.
Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.

title: Jailed Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years over foreign collusion
zh_title: 因勾结香港活动人士黄之锋被判十年徒刑
summary: 被监禁的香港民主活动人士黄之锋在承认串谋外国势力罪后被判处 10 年监禁，这是他根据北京实施的国家安全法第二次被定罪。黄之锋.资料照片：Studio Incendo。上个月在监狱中度过了30岁生日的黄周四在高等法院宣判时显得很平静。谭威廉法官表示，根据北京实施的国家安全法，他的罪行属于“性质严重”的罪行之一，该法可判处至少 10 年监禁。一辆惩教车抵达
content:
被监禁的香港民主活动人士黄之锋在承认串谋外国势力罪后被判处 10 年监禁，这是他根据北京实施的国家安全法第二次被定罪。黄之锋.资料照片：Studio Incendo。上个月在监狱中度过了30岁生日的黄周四在高等法院宣判时显得很平静。谭威廉法官表示，根据北京实施的国家安全法，他的罪行属于“性质严重”的罪行之一，该法可判处至少 10 年监禁。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在民主活动人士黄之锋宣判之前，一辆惩教车抵达高等法院。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。黄目前正在具有里程碑意义的“香港47”案件中因串谋颠覆国家政权而被判处四年零八个月的监禁，该案中45名著名的民主运动人士被定罪，并于2024年被判处最高10年监禁。谭法官下令，他新的10年刑期与他现有刑期的剩余两个月同时执行。这意味着黄可能会一直待在监狱里，直到 2036 年年满 40 岁，除非他获得减刑。在香港，国家安全囚犯因表现良好而需要提前释放，面临着更高的门槛。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在民主活动人士黄之锋宣判之前，警察在高等法院外巡逻。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
他自 2020 年 11 月以来一直被当局拘留，当时他承认在 2019 年抗议期间煽动和组织警察总部外未经授权的集会。“主谋”黄被指控与自我流亡的活动人士罗冠聪和其他未透露姓名的人士在 2020 年密谋，要求外国对香港和中国大陆政府实施制裁和封锁，或从事其他敌对活动。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，黄之锋被判刑后，高等法院外的警察。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。两人都是现已解散的民主党众志的联合创始人，在 2019 年的抗议和骚乱之后，他们卷入了“国际战线”。检察官表示，他们游说美国通过《香港人权与民主法案》等立法。 2026 年 11 月 5 日，在民主活动人士黄之锋宣判之前，支持者聚集在高等法院外。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。谭法官周四表示，黄和罗是犯罪行为的“头目”和“主谋”，他们在2019年和2020年倡导国际制裁，“加剧”了当时的政治危机，当时香港正卷入有争议的引渡法案引发的抗议和骚乱。
法官表示：“犯罪发生时，香港正在应对当地发生的社会动乱；被告为了达到自己的政治目的，伙同外国政府或外部势力勾结，加剧了香港的局势。”谭以13年监禁为起始刑期，并因黄及时认罪而减刑三年，但没有为入狱的活动人士提供任何进一步的折扣。他补充说：“虽然对被告的刑罚非常重，但处罚必须符合所犯罪行的严重性。”黄之锋被判刑后，领事馆代表在高等法院

【原文 English Original】
Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment after pleading guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law. Joshua Wong. File photo: Studio Incendo. Wong, who turned 30 in prison last month, appeared calm on Thursday as his sentence was handed down at the High Court. Judge William Tam said his offence was one of a “grave nature” under the Beijing-imposed national security law, which warrants a minimum of 10 years’ imprisonment. A Correctional Services van arrives at the High Court ahead of the sentencing of pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wong is currently serving a four-year, eight-month jail term for conspiracy to subvert state power in the landmark “Hong Kong 47” case , in which 45 prominent pro-democracy campaigners were convicted and sentenced to up to 10 years in jail in 2024. Judge Tam ordered that his new 10-year prison term run concurrently with the remaining two months of his existing sentence. That means Wong is likely to remain behind bars until 2036, when he turns 40, unless he receives sentence remission. In Hong Kong, national security prisoners face a higher threshold to secure early release for good behaviour. Police patrol outside the High Court ahead of the sentencing of pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. He has been held by authorities since November 2020, when he pleaded guilty to inciting and organising an unauthorised assembly outside police headquarters during the 2019 protests. ‘Masterminds’ Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and other unnamed individuals in 2020 to request that foreign countries impose sanctions and blockades, or engage in other hostile activities, directed against the governments of Hong Kong and mainland China. Police officers outside the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The pair, both co-founders of the now-disbanded pro-democracy party Demosisto, had engaged in an “international battlefront” in the wake of the 2019 protests and unrest. They lobbied for the passing of legislation such as the US’s Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, prosecutors said. Supporters gather outside the High Court ahead of the sentencing of pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Calling Wong and Law “ring-leaders” and “masterminds” of the offence, Judge Tam said on Thursday that their advocacy for international sanctions in 2019 and 2020 had “aggravated” the political crisis at the time, as Hong Kong was embroiled in protests and unrest triggered by a controversial extradition bill. “The offence took place at a time when Hong Kong was coping with the social turmoil that was happening locally; and in order to achieve their own political aims, the defendant, together with [Law] and their affiliates, exacerbated that situation in Hong Kong by colluding with foreign governments or external elements,” the judge said. Tam set 13 years’ imprisonment as a starting sentence and knocked off three years for Wong’s timely guilty plea, but did not offer any further discount to the jailed activist. “Whilst it is a very heavy sentence on the defendant, the punishment must fit the gravity of the crime committed,” he added. Consulate representatives at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wong said “thank you” and waved to his supporters, who crowded around the dock as he was led away by prison guards after the sentencing. Some were in tears as they called out words of support to the jailed activist. Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin, former members of Scholarism, the disbanded student activism group that Wong co-founded in 2011, left the High Court after the hearing and declined to comment. Former Scholarism activists Louis Lee and Tiffany Chin at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “As his friends, we need time to process this,” Chin told reporters in Cantonese. Security law In February, media mogul Jimmy Lai was sentenced to 20 years in jail for conspiring to collude with foreign forces, while three former executives of his Apple Daily newspaper were given 10-year prison terms. Beijing inserted national security legislation directly into Hong Kong’s mini-constitution in June 2020 following a year of pro-democracy protests and unrest. It criminalised subversion, secession, collusion with foreign forces and terrorist acts – broadly defined to include disruption to transport and other infrastructure. The move gave police sweeping new powers and led to hundreds of arrests amid new legal precedents , while dozens of civil society groups disappeared . The authorities say it restored stability and peace to the city, rejecting criticism from trade partners , the UN and NGOs .

title: Hong Kong lawmaker proposes digital ID checks for housing estate votes to combat bid-rigging
zh_title: 香港立法会议员提议对住宅区投票进行数字身份检查以打击串通投标
summary: 一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议采取了这样的形式
content:
一名香港立法会议员建议在遗产会议上投票时使用政府管理的数字平台来验证业主的身份，这一措施旨在帮助防止未经授权的代理投票。宏福苑.照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。立法会议员方恭蕙周三在立法会会议上提出了打击串通投标的提案，串通投标是建筑维修行业的一种反竞争行为，在大埔公寓大楼发生致命火灾近一年后，香港领导人李家超已将其定为刑事犯罪。她的建议以议员议案的形式提出，该议案由议员提出，无意产生立法效力，但可能敦促政府采取具体措施。根据立法会文件，方建议研究利用政府的“iAM Smart”数字平台建立电子机制来核实和确认业主身份，“从而防止伪造、未经授权签署授权书以及滥用代理投票等问题。”未经授权的投票 2021 年 12 月的一次会议上进行的未经授权的代理投票帮助任命了宏福苑翻修工程的项目顾问，去年 11 月发生导致 168 人死亡、数千人流离失所的火灾时，该工程正在进行中。
项目顾问 Will Power Architects 此后被当局起诉，并与工程承包商 Prestige Construction & Engineering 一起被列为火灾背后的“罪魁祸首”之一。Christine Fong 于 2026 年 1 月 1 日宣誓就任香港立法会第八届任期。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大约四分之一的代理选票是由时任区议员黄佩琪 (Peggy Wong) 收集的，她因在庄园中的角色受到指控以及缺席议会会议数月后于 9 月辞职。然而，根据调查的最终报告，向独立调查委员会提交的证据不足以证明她参与了大埔住宅区的串通投标。周三，曾任区议员的方议员在立法机关发表讲话时表示，她知道有人以当时身在海外的房主的名义在她所在地区的庄园进行投票，而他们并不知情。她在意见书中还敦促政府建立黑名单制度，禁止被判串标罪的当事人提交涉及公共资金和补贴的标书，以及须接受强制检查的建筑物项目。她还建议研究建立匿名电子招标系统，并利用人工智能和大数据建立招标“异常警报”系统。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong lawmaker has suggested using a government-managed digital platform to verify property owners’ identities when casting their ballots in estate meetings, a measure meant to help prevent unauthorised proxy voting. Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Lawmaker Christine Fong made the proposal at a Legislative Council (LegCo) meeting on Wednesday on combatting bid-rigging, an anti-competitive practice in the building maintenance industry that the city’s leader John Lee has moved to criminalise, almost a year after a deadly apartment complex fire in Tai Po. Her suggestion took the form of a member’s motion, a proposal introduced by a lawmaker that is not intended to have legislative effect but may urge the government to adopt specific measures. According to a LegCo document, Fong suggested looking into the use of the government’s “iAM Smart” digital platform to establish an electronic mechanism for verifying and confirming the identities of property owners, “thereby preventing issues such as forgery and unauthorized signing of powers of attorney and the abuse of proxy votes.” Unauthorised votes Unauthorised proxy votes cast at a December 2021 meeting helped appoint the project consultant for renovation works at Wang Fuk Court, which were ongoing at the time of the fire that killed 168 people and displaced thousands in November last year. Project consultant Will Power Architects has since been prosecuted by authorities and named as one of the “main culprits” behind the blaze, along with works contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering. Christine Fong is sworn in for the eighth term of Hong Kong’s Legislative Council on January 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. About a quarter of the proxy votes were collected by then-District Councillor Peggy Wong, who resigned from office in September amid allegations over her role at the estate and after months of absences at council meetings. However, evidence presented to an independent probe committee was insufficient to prove she was involved in bid-rigging at the Tai Po housing estate, according to the inquiry’s final report. Speaking at the legislature on Wednesday, lawmaker Fong, formerly a district councillor, said that she knew of votes being cast at estates in her district in the name of homeowners who were overseas at the time, without their knowledge. In her submission, she also urged the government to establish a blacklist system under which parties convicted of bid-rigging would be prohibited from submitting tenders involving public funds and subsidies, as well as projects for buildings subject to mandatory inspections. She also suggested looking into setting up an anonymised electronic tendering system and using artificial intelligence and big data to establish an “anomaly alert” system for tenders.

title: What the US midterms mean for ties with China
zh_title: 美国中期选举对中美关系意味着什么
summary: 分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。投票结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，投票结果可能会对特朗普产生以下影响：
content:
分析人士表示，民主党在本周的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，控制了国会，这对最大竞争对手中国来说既是机遇也是挑战。 2026 年 11 月 3 日，在佐治亚州亚特兰大举行的美国中期选举之夜派对上，民主党人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 预计将赢得佐治亚州州长竞选，支持者欢呼雀跃。照片：Erik S. Lesser/法新社。这次投票的结果让民主党有能力阻止唐纳德·特朗普总统特立独行的外交政策，它可能会如何影响华盛顿和北京之间的棘手关系：关税会受到限制吗？分析人士表示，赢得美国国会参众两院的控制权使民主党能够限制特朗普在其任期结束后的两年内对中国产品随意征收关税。这可能对特朗普来说是一个潜在的打击，在双方达成休战协议（定于一月到期）之前，特朗普在激烈的美中贸易战中一直履行职责。上海复旦大学国际问题研究院院长吴心伯表示，如果民主党限制特朗普，这意味着他“在与中国的谈判中将更难利用关税卡”。 2026 年 5 月 14 日，中国国家主席习近平（右）和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在北京人民大会堂会面。照片：中国外交部发言人毛宁，来自 Facebook。
然而，民主党人还必须权衡他们的行动与特朗普关税在美国企业中的受欢迎程度。新加坡南洋理工大学拉惹勒南国际研究学院高级研究员德鲁·汤普森表示，国会将“在未来两年内利用一切机会阻挠（特朗普的政策）”。但汤普森表示，民主党仍需谨慎对待进一步限制关税，这些关税“受到工会、蓝领工人和小企业的欢迎……他们历来是民主党的基础选民”。华盛顿布鲁金斯学会外交政策研究员帕特里夏·金(Patricia Kim)表示，国会将“不太愿意支持那些会急剧升级对华压力的措施，如果这样做可能会增加美国消费者和企业的成本或增加冲突的可能性”。台湾是“游戏规则改变者”？凯投宏观(Capital Economics)首席经济学家尼尔·希林(Neil Shearing)表示，台湾问题可能会“改变游戏规则”。台湾是美国支持的民主岛屿，北京声称拥有主权。华盛顿是台北最重要的安全支持者，已向台湾出售了价值数十亿美元的武器，台湾将用这些武器抵御中国潜在的攻击。但特朗普今年五月宣称美国对台军售可能成为与中国谈判的筹码，这让美国的立场受到质疑。此后，他的政府将一批价值 140 亿美元的武器推迟了数月。
台湾总统赖清德于 2026 年 2 月 11 日在台北举行的国防预算新闻发布会上发表讲话。照片：台湾总统府。希林在一份报告中写道，中国可以利用特朗普总统任期的剩余两年加大对台湾的压力，特别是如果北京“判断华盛顿心烦意乱，或者特朗普愿意同意不干预的条款”。特朗普最近赞扬了他与中国国家主席习近平的“伟大友谊”，迄今为止，他顶住了民主党人和一些共和党议员的政治压力，

【原文 English Original】
A sweeping victory for Democrats in US midterm elections this week, giving them control of Congress, presents both an opportunity and challenge for top rival China, analysts say. Supporters cheer after the announcement that Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, former mayor of Atlanta, is projected to win the Georgia gubernatorial race during a US midterm election night party in Atlanta, Georgia, on November 3, 2026. Photo: Erik S. Lesser/AFP. Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing: Will tariffs be limited? Winning control of both houses in the US Congress puts Democrats in a position to limit Trump’s liberal use of tariffs on Chinese products in the two years he has left in office, analysts say. That could be a potential blow to Trump, who has wielded duties throughout a frenzied US-China trade war before the two sides reached a truce, set to expire in January. If Democrats limit Trump, that means he “will be less able to leverage a tariff card in negotiations with China”, said Wu Xinbo, dean at the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University in Shanghai. China’s President Xi Jinping (right) and US President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on May 14, 2026. Photo: Mao Ning Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson, via Facebook. However, Democrats will also have to weigh their actions against the popularity of Trump’s tariffs among US businesses. Congress will “take every opportunity to thwart (Trump’s policies) over the next two years”, said Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University. But Democrats will still have to tread carefully on further restricting tariffs that “are popular with unions, blue-collar workers and small businesses… who have historically been a base constituency for the Democrats”, Thompson said. Congress will be “less inclined to support measures that would sharply escalate pressure on China if doing so risks raising costs for American consumers and businesses or increasing the likelihood of conflict”, said Patricia Kim, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution in Washington. Taiwan a ‘game changer’? The issue of Taiwan, the US-backed democratic island claimed by Beijing, could be a “game changer”, said Neil Shearing, group chief economist at Capital Economics. Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer and has sold billions of dollars’ worth of arms to Taiwan that the island would use to fend off a potential Chinese attack. But Trump threw the US stance into question in May when he declared that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip in talks with China. His administration has since delayed for months a $14-billion batch of weapons . Taiwan President Lai Ching-te speaks during a press conference on the defence budget in Taipei on February 11, 2026. Photo: Taiwan’s Office of the President. China could use the remaining two years of Trump’s presidency to increase pressure on Taiwan, particularly if Beijing “judges that Washington is distracted or that Trump would be willing to agree terms to not intervene”, Shearing wrote in a note. Trump, who recently hailed his “great friendship” with China’s President Xi Jinping, has so far resisted political pressure from Democrats — and some Republican lawmakers — to greenlight the arms package. But a Democrat-controlled Congress “may force Trump to resume arms sales to Taiwan next year”, Wu said. “If that happens, that will also undermine the stability of US-China relationship.” Alternatively, for China, renewed support of Taipei from the US Congress may be “a stronger incentive for (Beijing) to play it safer with Taiwan”, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute. Nevertheless, Thompson pointed out, while Congress can pass bills requiring Trump to approve an arms sale, the president retains the power to veto it “or simply ignore it”. Will Beijing treat Trump as a lame duck? From China’s perspective, even though Trump has been politically weakened by the midterms, Beijing is unlikely to change its strategy towards working with him, analysts say. “Beijing is likely to continue cultivating him through high-profile, leader-to-leader engagement with Xi Jinping, viewing this as the least costly way to manage relations with Washington,” said Kim. “Neither Beijing nor Washington appears to expect or seek a fundamental improvement in bilateral relations,” she added. Tsang of the SOAS China Institute said “Trump being relegated to lame-duck status will be used by the Chinese to put more pressure on him”. But, he added, Beijing is “calculating” and “would not want to push too hard and trigger Trump behaving totally irresponsibly”.

title: 涉中共境外介選 台退將臧幼俠等6人被法辦
summary: 台灣九合一地方選舉將至，圖為台北市長參選人沈伯洋（右）、蔣萬安（左）日前出席辯論會。（中央社） 【大紀元2026年11月05日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）台灣高雄地檢署偵辦中共境外勢力介入台灣選舉案，經訊問諭知被告退役少將臧幼俠等6人交保，並限制出境出海，臧幼俠因涉案嫌疑重大，裁定70萬元（新台幣，以下同）交保，其餘5人5萬至10萬元交保。 台灣高雄地檢署今天（5日）發布新聞稿指出，日前接獲法務部調查局屏東縣調查站提報境外勢力介入選舉情資，立即指派主任檢察官董秀菁、檢察官王
content:
台灣九合一地方選舉將至，圖為台北市長參選人沈伯洋（右）、蔣萬安（左）日前出席辯論會。（中央社）
【大紀元2026年11月05日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）台灣高雄地檢署偵辦中共境外勢力介入台灣選舉案，經訊問諭知被告退役少將臧幼俠等6人交保，並限制出境出海，臧幼俠因涉案嫌疑重大，裁定70萬元（新台幣，以下同）交保，其餘5人5萬至10萬元交保。
台灣高雄地檢署今天（5日）發布新聞稿指出，日前接獲法務部調查局屏東縣調查站提報境外勢力介入選舉情資，立即指派主任檢察官董秀菁、檢察官王建中組成專案小組全力搜證，經向法院聲請搜索票，共搜索14處、傳訊22人。
經檢方訊問後，諭知被告郭姓2人、盧姓1人、潘姓1人及袁姓女子1人等5人，分別以5萬至10萬元交保，並限制出境出海。另向法院聲請羈押被告臧幼俠，經法院審理認定臧男犯罪嫌疑重大，但無羈押必要，裁定70萬元交保，並限制出境出海。
檢方指出，臧幼俠是台灣振興中華民族文化暨經濟促進協會理事長、高雄市台灣振興中華民族文化暨經濟促進協會實際負責人，明知中國大陸「黃埔軍校同學會」是由中共中央統一戰線工作部直接指導與管理，為境外敵對勢力政府所屬組織，仍多次安排具有投票權民眾赴中，接受落地招待旅遊，並由中方全額提供食宿、交通、飲宴及參訪等費用，由各省統戰部、台辦及黃埔軍校同學會等官員安排接待。
經查被告多人也受到境外勢力資助及指示，今年在台灣舉辦多場餐會，要求到場參與者支持特定公職人員選舉的候選人，企圖影響2026年台灣地方公職人員選舉的公平性與結果。

title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail
zh_title: 香港民运人士黄之锋被判入狱10年
source: 菲律宾在中国紧张局势中加强其最北端的防御
summary: 香港民运人士黄之锋被判入狱10年 |法院新闻|半岛电视台分享 香港民主活动人士黄之锋在社交媒体上被判入狱 10 年 民主活动人士黄之锋于 2020 年首次入狱 [文件：法新社] 半岛电视台工作人员、法新社、美联社和路透社 自 2020 年以来一直入狱的香港民主活动人士黄之锋被追加监禁 10 年。香港高等法院周四裁定黄与外国实体勾结，违反香港国家安全法。 list 1 of 3Jimmy Lai 句子
content:
香港民运人士黄之锋被判入狱10年 |法院新闻|半岛电视台
分享 香港民主活动人士黄之锋在社交媒体上被判处 10 年监禁
民主活动家黄之锋于 2020 年首次入狱 [文件：法新社]
半岛电视台工作人员、法新社、美联社和路透社
自2020年起入狱的香港民主活动人士黄之锋被追加监禁10年。
香港高等法院周四裁定黄与外国实体勾结，违反香港国家安全法。
list 1 of 3 黎智英被判刑：其他香港民主抗议者怎么了？
名单 3 香港活动人士黄之锋在国家安全案件中认罪 2
list 3 of 3我们对被监禁的香港活动人士黄之锋最新指控的了解
该判决距离他预计于 2027 年 1 月获释仅两个月。
“惩罚必须与罪行的严重性相适应，”高等法院法官谭威廉在宣判时对挤满人的法庭说。
“法院也有必要表达社会对被告图谋并与他人勾结外国势力或外部势力危害国家安全的深恶痛绝。”
现年30岁的黄被指控与自流亡的活动人士罗冠聪等人密谋，要求中国境外的外国、机构或个人实施制裁或封锁，或从事其他针对政府的敌对活动。
他于九月承认了这项指控。谭说，他曾考虑以 13 年监禁为起点，但由于黄的认罪和减刑，将刑期减至 10 年。
黄曾是香港民主运动的代言人，自 2020 年以来一直入狱。他因一年前在抗议活动中所扮演的角色而入狱。
示威活动是由允许引渡到中国大陆的计划引发的，但很快演变成一场更广泛的民主运动。黄成为该运动的杰出代表，经常出现在新闻频道上。他后来承认煽动和组织未经授权的反政府集会罪。
各国政府和人权组织周四批评了法院的裁决。
美国驻香港领事馆表示，“强烈谴责”对黄的追加判决，并呼吁“立即释放”他。
领事馆发言人在给法新社的一份声明中表示：“黄自2020年12月以来一直被不公正地监禁，这表明北京将不遗余力地压制那些倡导香港基本自由的人。”
在他宣判后，台湾还批评了对香港民主活动人士的“无休止的政治迫害”。
台湾最高对华政策机构表示，北京和香港政府利用“独裁工具”“捏造罪名……进行无休止的政治迫害，压制人民追求自由、民主和人权的合法权利”。
人权观察谴责对黄的最新指控。 “对黄之锋毫无根据的指控作出严厉判决是残酷和不公正的。推动社会变革的年轻人是任何充满活力的社会的财富，但香港政府将他们关进监狱，”该组织亚洲区总监伊莱恩·皮尔森(Elaine Pearson)表示。
国际特赦组织也批评对黄的额外判刑，称这是“再次严峻地提醒我们，香港的国家安全法已成为压制香港的工具”。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail | Courts News | Al Jazeera
Share Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail on social media
Pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was first imprisoned in 2020 [File: AFP]
By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP, AP and Reuters
Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong, who has been in prison since 2020, has been jailed for an additional 10 years.
Hong Kong’s High Court found Wong guilty of colluding with foreign entities in violation of the city’s national security law on Thursday.
list 1 of 3Jimmy Lai sentenced: What happened to other HK pro-democracy protesters?
list 2 of 3Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in national security case
list 3 of 3What we know about jailed HK activist Joshua Wong’s latest charge
The sentence comes just two months before he was expected to be released in January 2027.
“The punishment must fit the gravity of ⁠the crime,” High Court Judge William Tam told a packed courtroom while delivering the sentence.
“It is also necessary for the court to express the community’s abhorrence of the defendant’s scheme and acts with others to collude with foreign forces or external elements to endanger national security.”
Wong, now 30, was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and others to ask foreign countries, bodies or individuals outside China to impose sanctions or blockades, or engage in other hostile activities against the government.
He pleaded guilty to the charge in September. Tam said he considered a 13-year prison sentence as a starting point but reduced it to 10 because of Wong’s guilty plea and mitigation.
Wong was once the face of Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement and has been in jail since 2020. He was imprisoned over his role in protests held a year earlier.
The demonstrations were prompted by plans to allow extradition to mainland China but soon evolved into a wider pro-democracy movement. Wong became a prominent representative of the movement, regularly appearing on news channels. He later pleaded guilty to inciting and organising an unauthorised antigovernment assembly.
Governments and rights groups criticised the court’s decision on Thursday.
The United States consulate in Hong Kong said that it “strongly condemns” the additional sentence handed to Wong, and called for his “immediate release”.
“Wong has been unjustly imprisoned since December 2020, demonstrating that Beijing will go to extraordinary lengths to silence those who advocate for fundamental freedoms in Hong Kong,” a consulate spokesperson said in a statement to the AFP news agency.
After his sentencing, Taiwan also criticised the “endless political persecution” of Hong Kong pro-democracy activists.
Beijing and the Hong Kong government use “authoritarian tools” to “fabricate charges … engage in endless political persecution, and suppress the people’s legitimate rights to pursue freedom, democracy, and human rights,” Taiwan’s top China policy body said.
Human Rights Watch denounced the latest charge against Wong. “The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust. Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars,” said Elaine Pearson, the group’s Asia director.
Amnesty International also criticised Wong’s additional sentence, saying it was “another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent”.

zh_title: 香港黄之锋：从青少年抗议领袖到入狱十年
summary: 香港黄之锋：从青少年抗议领袖到入狱十年香港《海峡时报》黄之锋：从青少年抗议领袖到坐牢十年这是数十年来对中国共产党领导人最大胆的民粹主义挑战，周四被判处 10 年以上监禁。黄自202年起就入狱
content:
香港黄之锋：从青少年抗议领袖到入狱十年海峡时报
香港黄之锋：从青少年抗议领袖到入狱十年
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发表于 2026 年 11 月 5 日 下午 04:57
更新于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，下午 05:23
香港，11 月 5 日 - 香港民主活动家黄之锋周四被判处 10 年以上监禁。黄之锋曾是 2014 年雨伞运动的领导人，该运动对中国共产党领导人提出了数十年来最大胆的民粹主义挑战之一。
黄自2020年以来一直入狱，根据亚洲金融中心的国家安全法，他承认了与外国实体勾结的指控。
当他出狱时，他已经年近40岁了，这与1997年他还是一个一岁小孩的日子相去甚远，当时英国将他的城市交还给中国，并承诺给予广泛的自治权以及言论和集会自由。
“一名国家安全官员说他和我是‘敌人’，并感叹他因为我而失去了很多朋友，”黄周四回忆起他被指控的那天说道。
“我回答说：‘你不是我的敌人。我们都是香港人；我们之间没有对抗，’”他在缓和评论中补充道。
黄的激进主义之旅始于年仅 14 岁，当时他与他人共同创立了一个名为“学民思潮”的组织，该组织举行了大规模抗议活动，并最终迫使政府搁置了在学校实施的亲中国国民教育计划，从而登上了香港的民主舞台。
17 岁时，黄是一个留着碗形头发、戴着黑框眼镜的瘦削青年，成为了民主派“雨伞运动”的国际代言人，指的是抗议者如何抵御防暴警察发射的催泪瓦斯和胡椒喷雾。
黄的激进主义和直言不讳的异议使他多次入狱，尤其是在雨伞运动高峰期吸引了数十万抗议者，导致市中心街道瘫痪79天之后。
在最新案件中，检察官指控黄在 2020 年 7 月至 11 月期间与其他人勾结，寻求外国制裁或针对香港和中国的敌对行动。
尽管他承认了这一指控，但黄说，他错误地认为自己的行为符合法律，并补充说，他从未主张香港独立或中国崩溃。
这些事件的时间框架至关重要，因为在 2019 年持续数月有时甚至是暴力的民主抗议活动之后，北京于当年 6 月下旬对香港实施了《国家安全法》。
该法律实际上取缔了黄和他的同僚曾经认为理所当然的许多政治活动，或将其置于危险之中。
黄成为国际舞台上的熟悉面孔，也是北京和香港当局的眼中钉，2014 年登上《时代》杂志封面，2017 年出现在 Netflix 纪录片中，记录了他的政治生涯。
他与包括媒体大亨黎智英在内的其他香港批评中国大陆的人一起多次被提名诺贝尔和平奖。

Hong Kong's Joshua Wong: From teenage protest leader to a decade behind bars | The Straits Times
Hong Kong's Joshua Wong: From teenage protest leader to a decade behind bars
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 05, 2026, 04:57 PM
Updated Nov 05, 2026, 05:23 PM
HONG KONG, Nov 5 - Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong, once a leader of the 2014 Umbrella Movement that posed one of the boldest populist challenges to the leaders of China's Communist Party in decades, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 more years in jail.
Wong, who has been behind bars since 2020, pleaded guilty to a charge of collusion with foreign entities under the Asian financial hub's national security law, ushered in that year.
He will be approaching 40 when he leaves jail, a long way off from his days as a one-year-old toddler in 1997, when Britain handed his city back to China with a promise of extensive autonomy and freedom of speech and assembly.
"One national security officer said he and I were 'enemies' and lamented that he had lost many friends because of me," Wong said on Thursday, recalling the day he was charged.
"I replied: 'You are not my enemy. We are all Hong Kongers; there is no antagonism between us,'" he added in his mitigation comments.
Wong's activist journey started at just 14, as he emerged on Hong Kong's democratic stage by co-founding a group called Scholarism that held mass protests and ultimately forced the government to shelve plans for a pro-China national education scheme in schools.
By age 17, as a thin youth with bowl-cut hair and dark-rimmed glasses, Wong was the international face of the pro-democracy "Umbrella Movement", referring to how protesters warded off riot police volleys of tear gas and pepper spray.
Wong's activism and vocal dissent landed him in jail numerous times, not least after the Umbrella Movement drew hundreds of thousands of protesters at its peak to paralyse streets in the city's heart for 79 days.
Prosecutors in the latest case accused Wong of working along with others to solicit foreign sanctions or hostile actions against Hong Kong and China between July and November 2020.
Though he pleaded guilty to the charge, Wong said he mistakenly thought his actions were within the law, adding that he had never advocated Hong Kong independence nor the collapse of China.
The timeframe of the events is key, since Beijing in late June of that year had imposed the National Security Law on the city following months of sometimes-violent pro-democracy protests in 2019.
The law effectively outlawed or put at risk many of the political activities that Wong and his peers once took for granted.
Wong became a familiar face on the international scene and a thorn in the side of authorities in Beijing and Hong Kong, featuring on the front cover of Time magazine in 2014 and in a Netflix documentary in 2017 that chronicled his political life.
Along with other Hong Kong critics of mainland China, including media tycoon Jimmy Lai, he was repeatedly nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize.
He made it a mission to drum up support for Hong Kong's democracy movement at home and overseas, meeting politicians from the United States and Europe, drawing the wrath of Beijing, which called him a "black hand" of foreign forces.
Outsiders who met him during this time recall his striking air of quiet determination, and apparently unshakable convictions.
When Wong left jail in June 2019 at the height of the protests, he was not a leading figure in organising the rallies, but he once again became one of the movement's most globally recognised faces.
Scholarism had morphed into Demosisto, a political party that once backed a referendum on Hong Kong's sovereignty and installed the youngest candidate ever on the city's Legislative Council before he was disqualified.
Demosisto was disbanded within hours after the National Security Law was passed.
In 2017, just before another sentencing, Wong told more than 100 supporters who thronged the court lobby, some weeping, that he had no regrets.
"I hope Hong Kong people won't give up," he said. "Victory is ours. When we are released next year I hope we can see a Hong Kong that is full of hope. I want to see Hong Kong people not giving up. This is my last wish before I go to jail."
Nearly 10 years on, Wong's extended term in prison is the latest blow for a movement whose followers find themselves in detention, exile or, in the case of some, cowed into silence.
Standing in the dock on Thursday, Wong was silent as the judge sentenced him to 10 years in jail that will keep him in prison after his current term ends in January. The sentence will be served concurrently, effectively shortening it by two months.
Wong mentioned a desire to eventually look after his ageing parents above all.
This, along with the fact that books on Chinese history and Hong Kong's mini-constitution were among the hundreds he was reading in jail, prompted the judge to hail Wong's efforts at rehabilitation as "commendable". REUTERS

消息人士称，印度正在进行最后阶段谈判，以扩大对菲律宾的布拉莫斯导弹销售

自 2025 年印度和巴基斯坦之间为期四天的冲突以来，人们对布拉莫斯系统的兴趣有所增加。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，下午 05:35
更新于 2026 年 11 月 5 日，下午 05:35
印度正在就扩大对菲律宾的布拉莫斯导弹销售进行最后谈判，涉及约五个系统和近 60 枚导弹。这笔交易可能价值7亿美元至8亿美元。
随着与中国在南海的紧张局势加剧，马尼拉希望部署更多的布拉莫斯部队来加强其军事和海岸防御。菲律宾官员表示，小费迪南德·马科斯总统希望获得更多导弹。
布拉莫斯由印度和俄罗斯制造，是一种可用于陆地、海上和空中的快速巡航导弹。印度还推动向其他国家出口导弹，国防出口增长62%，达到3842.4亿卢比。
新德里/马尼拉 — — 三名直接了解此事的消息人士告诉路透社，印度正就扩大向菲律宾出售超音速巡航导弹进行最后阶段谈判，新德里即将完成 2022 年协议下的交付。
两名印度消息人士称，菲律宾预计将购买约 5 个布拉莫斯系统，总共近 60 枚导弹，这笔交易可能价值 7 亿美元（893.38 新元）至 8 亿美元。
一位印度消息人士称：“马尼拉再次表现出购买大约五套布拉莫斯导弹系统的兴趣，他们现在将印度视为非常可靠的合作伙伴。”
随着有争议的南海紧张局势加剧，新德里与菲律宾最新可能达成的协议远高于上次价值3.75亿美元的布拉莫斯海军订单。
布拉莫斯由印度和俄罗斯联合开发，是世界上速度最快的巡航导弹之一，可以从陆地、海上和空中平台发射。
菲律宾国防部发言人阿森尼奥·安多隆告诉路透社，小费迪南德·马科斯总统已表达了购买更多布拉莫斯导弹的愿望。安多隆没有提供更多细节。
菲律宾国防部长吉尔伯托·特奥多罗在 11 月 4 日举行的德里防务对话上发表虚拟讲话时表示，菲律宾希望获得更多的“布拉莫斯”系统，并与印度当局分享了一份愿望清单，以使该系统更适合菲律宾的环境。
此次额外购买正值马尼拉正在增强军事实力之际，两国因南海主权主张重叠而导致与北京的紧张局势升级，两国近年来在南海发生冲突。
印度国防部和外交部以及导弹制造商布拉莫斯航空航天公司没有回应置评请求。
自2025年印度和巴基斯坦之间为期四天的冲突以来，人们对布拉莫斯系统的兴趣有所增加，当时印度首次在战斗中使用了该武器系统。
今年7月，德里宣布向印度尼西亚供应布拉莫斯导弹，并与越南签署了协议。它正在与阿联酋、泰国、南非和巴西等其他一些国家就该系统进行谈判。
政府数据显示，截至 3 月份的财年，印度的国防出口达到 3842.4 亿卢比（51.9 亿新元），比上年同期增长超过 62%。

India in talks to expand BrahMos sale to Philippines | The Straits Times
India in final-stage talks to expand BrahMos missile sale to Philippines, sources say
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Interest in the BrahMos system has increased since the four-day conflict between India and Pakistan in 2025.
Published Nov 05, 2026, 05:35 PM
Updated Nov 05, 2026, 05:35 PM
India is in final talks to expand BrahMos missile sales to the Philippines, with about five systems and nearly 60 missiles. The deal may be worth US$700 million to US$800 million.
Manila wants more BrahMos units to strengthen its military and coastal defences as tensions rise with China in the South China Sea. Philippine officials said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr wants more missiles.
BrahMos, made by India and Russia, is a fast cruise missile used from land, sea and air. India is also pushing missile exports to other countries, and defence exports rose 62% to 384.24 billion rupees.
NEW DELHI/MANILA – India is in final-stage talks to expand its sale of supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under a 2022 deal.
The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems, nearly 60 missiles in total, in a deal potentially worth US$700 million (S$893.38) to US$800 million, two of the Indian sources said.
“Manila has shown interest again to procure about five systems of the BrahMos and they now view India as a very reliable partner,” one Indian source said.
New Delhi’s latest likely deal with the Philippines, which is modernising its military and strengthening coastal defences as tensions rise in the disputed South China Sea, is much higher than the last US$375 million order of BrahMos for naval use.
BrahMos, developed jointly by India and Russia, is among the world’s fastest cruise missiles and can be launched ​from land, sea and air platforms.
Arsenio Andolong, Philippines defence ministry spokesperson, told Reuters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles. Andolong did not offer more details.
Speaking virtually at the Delhi Defence Dialogue on Nov 4, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the Philippines hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with the Indian authorities to make the system more tailored to the Philippine environment.
The additional purchase comes at a time when Manila is building its military strength as tension escalates with Beijing on overlapping claims in the South China Sea, where the two countries have clashed in recent years.
India’s defence and ​foreign ministries, as well as missile maker BrahMos Aerospace, did not respond to requests for comment.
Interest in the BrahMos system has increased since the four-day conflict between India and Pakistan in 2025, when India used the weapons system for the first time in battle.
In July, Delhi announced the supply of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia and has also signed a deal with Vietnam. It is in talks on the system with a number of other countries including UAE, Thailand, South Africa and Brazil.
India’s defence exports for the fiscal year to March reached 384.24 billion rupees (S$5.19 billion), ​a jump of more than 62% from the ‌same period the year before, government data showed.

content:
日本否认寻求将缅甸从黑名单中删除 - 日本时报
日本否认寻求将缅甸从黑名单中删除
缅甸政变头目后来成为总统敏昂莱。缅甸于 2022 年被列入金融行动特别工作组的黑名单，因为该国在军事政变后陷入动荡和广泛的内战。 |路透社
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads 电子邮件 打印 书签故事 复制链接
日本财务省否认推动将缅甸从全球金融监管机构的黑名单中删除，上周有报道称缅甸是支持将其从黑名单中删除的国家之一。
缅甸于 2022 年被列入金融行动特别工作组 (FATF) 的黑名单，因为该国在军事政变后陷入动荡和广泛的内战。黑名单要求各国对与缅甸的金融交易加强筛查，以避免洗钱和恐怖主义融资。
日本外务省在给记者的一份声明中表示：“日本政府并没有试图将缅甸从 FATF 黑名单中删除。” “日本希望缅甸做出必要的改进，加强打击洗钱及相关非法活动的措施。”
10 月 30 日，这个由 40 名成员组成的全球机构在巴黎举行闭门会议后，缅甸仍留在黑名单上。日本厚生省在声明中表示，日本并未在巴黎会议上表示希望将缅甸从黑名单中删除。
据日本政府高级官员和另一位知情人士透露，10月30日有报道称，日本正在推动缅甸的移除。周四联系到的其中一位人士表示，他们坚持自己的评论，而另一位人士则无法立即联系到置评。
缅甸军方支持的政府发言人周六在一条消息中表示，各个“友好国家”正在支持其从名单中删除的努力。
“美国、中国、日本、印度、韩国和印度尼西亚认可缅甸的努力。我们感谢他们所有人认可缅甸目前取得的进展，”发言人补充道，但没有详细说明。
韩国外交部表示，“鼓励缅甸遵守金融行动特别工作组的职责，并就这一问题与金融行动特别工作组成员国密切协调”。
该部表示，政府“正在努力加强尚未完全实施金融行动特别工作组标准的国家打击洗钱和恐怖主义融资的能力”。
发言人点名的所有其他国家要么拒绝置评，要么没有回应置评请求。
日本否认正在推动将缅甸从名单中删除，缅甸军方支持的政府没有立即发表评论。

Japan denies seeking Myanmar’s removal from blacklist
Myanmar's coup chief turned president, Min Aung Hlaing. Myanmar was placed on the Financial Action Task Force's blacklist in 2022 as the country was plunged into turmoil and widespread civil war following a military coup. | REUTERS
X Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Threads Email Print Bookmark story Copy link
Japan’s Ministry of Finance has denied pushing for Myanmar to be removed from a global financial watchdog’s blacklist after a report said last week that it was among countries supporting the removal.
Myanmar was added to the Financial Action Task Force’s (FATF) blacklist in 2022 as the country was plunged into turmoil and widespread civil war following a military coup. The blacklist requires countries to apply enhanced screening to financial transactions with Myanmar to avoid money laundering and terrorist financing.
“There is no fact that the Japanese government sought to have Myanmar removed from the FATF blacklist,“ the ministry said in a statement to reporters. “Japan hopes that Myanmar will make the necessary improvements to strengthen its measures against money laundering and related illicit activities.”
Myanmar remained on the blacklist following a closed-door meeting of the 40-member global body in Paris on Oct. 30. Japan did not state at the Paris meeting that it wanted Myanmar removed, the ministry said in its statement.
It was reported on Oct. 30 that Japan was pushing for Myanmar’s removal, according to a senior Japanese government official and another person familiar with the matter. One of the people, reached on Thursday, said they stood by their comments, while the other could not be immediately reached for comment.
A spokesperson for Myanmar’s military-backed government said in a message on Saturday that various “friendly countries” were supporting its efforts to be removed from the list.
“The United States, China, Japan, India, South Korea and Indonesia recognize Myanmar’s efforts. We are grateful to all of them for acknowledging Myanmar’s current progress,” the spokesperson added, without elaborating.
South Korea’s foreign ministry said it was “encouraging Myanmar to abide by FATF duties, and closely coordinating with FATF member countries on the issue.”
The government “is making efforts to strengthen the capabilities of countries that have not fully implemented FATF standards to combat money laundering and terrorist financing,” the ministry said.
All the other countries named by the spokesperson either declined to comment or did not respond to a request for comment.
Myanmar’s military-backed government did not immediately have comment on Japan’s denial that it was pushing to have Myanmar removed from the list.
